  PROBLEM: A failed `gh issue edit` could still advance the readiness-refresh path against a stale tracker body, yielding a false-positive `orchestrator/integration-pr-not-ready=success`.
  WHY: The tightened guard now requires either a successful body change or an already-synced hash before refreshing, so the stale-body success path is closed.

  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: Using `\s` in the grep regex is GNU-only and can break template-body detection on BSD grep.
  WHY: `[[:space:]]` is POSIX-compliant and avoids the silent failure mode on macOS.

  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The `if issue is None` branch was unreachable after the partial-override refactor.
  WHY: The earlier error handling already returns before this branch, so removing it is dead-code cleanup.

  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]

  WHY: The test injects `fail_issue_edit_for=[192]` and asserts `commit_status_posts` stays empty while `tracking_body_sync_hash` and `tracking_body_last_readiness_refresh_hash` remain stale.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2428-2431 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The readiness refresh condition now correctly gates on successful edit or already-synced-but-not-yet-refreshed state, preventing false-positive success status posts when `gh issue edit` fails
  WHY: Before the fix, if `gh issue edit` failed, the code could still proceed to refresh `orchestrator/integration-pr-not-ready` using the locally rendered `desired_body_file` instead of the still-stale live tracker body, incorrectly reporting the integration PR as "ready".
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2384 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Changed `\s` to `[[:space:]]` in the grep regex.
  WHY: The previous regex would fail on BSD grep (macOS), causing the template body detection to fail silently and potentially skip reconciliation.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:207-212 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Removed unreachable `if issue is None` check after the new partial-override logic.
  WHY: After the refactoring to support `--tracking-body-file` and `--tracking-labels-file` overrides, the earlier error handling on lines 199-201 already returns, making this code unreachable.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:4058-4128 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Added regression test `test_tracking_body_reconcile_skips_readiness_refresh_when_issue_body_edit_fails` that verifies when `gh issue edit` fails, no readiness refresh occurs and state hashes remain unchanged.
  WHY: The test correctly injects failure via `fail_issue_edit_for=[192]` and asserts that `commit_status_posts` is empty and both `tracking_body_sync_hash` and `tracking_body_last_readiness_refresh_hash` remain at their stale values.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~2405, ~2431-2435 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `reconcile_tracking_issue_body_from_state` path now correctly guards readiness refresh behind a successful body edit (or already-synced hash), eliminating the false-positive `orchestrator/integration-pr-not-ready=success` that could have been posted against a stale live tracker body.
  WHY: Previously a transient `gh issue edit` failure could leave the live body stale while the state hash moved forward, causing later poll ticks to skip the retry; the tightened condition closes that exact path.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
